analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/ssd-write-queue-six-jobs.md) and an update to the write-behind queue rows in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head lines 296-297; base line 296). The Swift code that sets writeQueueMaxJobs from 2 to 6 is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. I checked the documented behavior against T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix-cache tier, A-001) and T-010 (availability).

For attention blocks, the documented queue limit rises from 2 to 6 jobs. The queued-byte cap is unchanged: max(512 MiB, maxStageBytes + 256 MiB), which is 1,280 MiB at the default stage cap. Host memory therefore stays bounded by the existing cap. Overflow still drops the donation as write_queue_full, so live serving is not blocked.

For complete checkpoints, the docs describe no queued-byte cap. Queued jobs reference donor state that stays charged to the engine admission ledger. Process-memory-owner or diffusion-layout donations reserve 20 MiB of I/O scratch and settle host_memory_unavailable if refused. The changelog states plainly that up to six donors, each holding KV memory, can now wait on a write backlog, and that stream end is delayed until their checkpoints settle. This is a small availability and memory-retention trade-off, up from 2 donors. Retention is bounded by the ledgers and queue depth, and I found no evidence of an unbounded regression or a new trust-boundary change. The remaining question is whether the code actually enforces those ledger charges, since I could not confirm it.

On disk, the change adds no new fields, key derivation, TTL, scope handling or plaintext metadata. The T-041 posture (HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, write caps) is unaffected. The daily write cap and the demand and rate-limit gates still bound SSD wear.

The integration pass should confirm in SSDPrefixCachePolicy.swift, SSDWriteBehind.swift, SSDHybridCheckpointStore.swift and EngineLoopV2.swift that the byte cap and memory charging match the docs. It should also confirm that a donor stuck behind a stalled writer cannot hold KV memory indefinitely, for example through cancellation, close or a disk-stall timeout.
